Pre-scan artifact: this string is the tail of the headline running into the opening words 'By the reviewer's account'. It is not an entity claim at all and nothing in it is unsupported.

claims.claim: Discovery here is something that happens to a person who is walking around Edinburgh in August
claims.reason: The source never states when the festival takes place. 'in August' is an invented temporal detail imported from outside knowledge of the Edinburgh festival calendar; the source text supplies no month, date, or season.

claims.claim: And that second obligation is harder to discharge, because the subject is not in the room to say whether it has been met.
claims.reason: Two unsupported moves stated as settled. The source's single sentence about a 'duty - to viewers and to their subjects - to tell them clearly' ranks nothing and offers no comparison of difficulty; 'harder to discharge' is the article's own evaluative conclusion presented as fact. The 'because' clause then supplies a causal explanation the source never gives, and generalises that subjects are absent or unable to respond - true of George, Walter and Hasegawa, but not established by the source for the festival's subjects as a class (Rothschild, Hardy, Maguire, Alrai, Fitzpatrick, Wood and Edelstein are all presented as living, exhibiting artists).

claims.claim: By the reviewer's account, the Edinburgh art festival is something you move through rather than read.
claims.reason: Attributed to the reviewer, but the reviewer never frames the festival this way. The source supports 'big, unwieldy, confusing' and 'impossible to figure out how any of it fits together'; the move-through-rather-than-read opposition is the article's interpretive gloss wearing the reviewer's attribution. Resolvable only if the source elsewhere states this framing, which the given text does not.

The source says only that it is 'impossible to figure out how any of it fits together'. It says nothing about a map, guide, or programme existing or failing. The sentence introduces an object not present in the source and asserts that it fails; verifying it would require the source to mention festival wayfinding material.
